raw_response:
I’m farming only 5 mu, and some people in my family work outside, so I can’t spread myself too thin. On my land, I still want the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way to keep grain and income. But I also keep some cotton and peanut, because if grain price is weak or one crop has a bad year, I still have something else to rely on. I finished middle school, so I do listen to extension advice, but in the end I still follow what has worked on my own fields. This year I will keep inputs in the middle range, not too low, because saving a little money on fertilizer is not worth a clear yield loss. But I also won’t push too hard, because pumping water costs money and my family labor is limited.

For the 2 mu under wheat-maize, I’ll manage wheat first with one spring topdress and about 2 irrigations if rainfall is not enough, then plant summer maize right after wheat harvest with as little delay as possible. Cotton I’ll keep on 1.5 mu because it can bring cash, but it needs more watching, so I won’t expand it. Peanut I’ll put on 1.5 mu because it is manageable, doesn’t need as much fertilizer N, and helps spread risk. I’ll use improved seed where it matters, do normal tillage, and only spray when I really see weed, insect, or disease pressure.
